extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) registered to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; USPTO counsel
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO disciplinary standards for patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order / settlement describing factual findings, legal conclusions, and sanctions for a registered patent practitioner's alleged violations of USPTO disciplinary rules, protective order obligations, and IDS/reexamination filing duties. Useful as guidance on practitioner responsibilities when handling confidential litigation materials and filing IDSs in USPTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of USPTO Director over practitioner discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against registered practitioners are within the Director's authority and governed by the cited statutory and regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent practitioner is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners must comply with the Code's standards of conduct in all matters before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in reexamination (IDS obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 1.933(a) and 37 C.F.R. § 1.555(a) impose a duty of disclosure upon 'each individual associated with the patent owner' in a reexamination to submit potentially material information (e.g., prior art) in an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals associated with the patent owner must disclose potentially material prior art in reexamination proceedings to avoid inequitable-conduct-related issues; the IDS assembled here included numerous documents the practitioner believed to be material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for filing confidential documents with the USPTO (MPEP § 724.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential documents submitted to the USPTO must be filed following the procedures set forth in MPEP § 724.02 to preserve confidentiality; failure to follow those procedures can make the documents publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The other practitioner filed IDS documents without following MPEP § 724.02, causing the 56 documents to become available for public inspection until interim sealing; practitioners should use MPEP procedures to protect confidential submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective order sealing and in-court disclosure procedures (paragraphs 6 & 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The protective order required designated confidential documents to be submitted to the court in a sealed envelope or other appropriate sealed container with certain markings (paragraph 6) and required notice to opposing counsel and the court prior to any in-court disclosure so the court may determine handling (paragraph 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documents are subject to protective-order confidentiality, parties must follow the order's sealing and notice procedures before revealing them at trial or filing them under seal; failure to satisfy those procedures can undermine confidentiality claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on recipients of 'CONFIDENTIAL - NON-PROSECUTING ATTORNEY EYES ONLY' materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The protective order prohibited disclosure or communication of materials labeled 'CONFIDENTIAL - NON-PROSECUTING ATTORNEY EYES ONLY' to more than three specifically designated persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure to persons not designated (e.g., another practitioner) violates the protective order's express recipient limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on use of designated discovery materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated discovery materials were required to be received and used only for purposes directly related to the suit and not for any other purpose (including proceedings before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such materials in other fora (e.g., USPTO reexamination) without compliance with the protective order is prohibited and may constitute a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-month bar on prosecution involvement after access to confidential materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The protective order prohibited attorneys who had access to confidential documents from substantive involvement in the preparation or prosecution of related patent applications for twelve (12) months after the case's determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorneys given access to certain confidential materials must refrain from prosecuting related patent matters for the specified statutory period to avoid conflicts or misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to employ reasonable measures to control confidential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside counsel of record were required to be responsible for employing reasonable measures to control duplication of, access to, and distribution of confidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel must implement and enforce reasonable safeguards and access controls for protected materials; failure to do so supports findings of violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations after unauthorized disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The party responsible for an unauthorized disclosure must, as soon as practicable after learning of the disclosure: (a) inform the other party in writing of all pertinent facts relating to the disclosure, (b) use its best efforts to retrieve the material or information, and (c) make every effort to prevent further disclosure by the unauthorized person(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification, retrieval efforts, and remedial steps are required; omission of these steps is itself a failure to comply with protective-order remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to seek court relief when protective-order issues cannot be resolved
rubrics_metrics.description: The protective order stated that parties are required to move the district court for relief when they are unable to resolve an issue related to a potential violation of the protective order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about applicability or proper handling of protected materials, practitioners should seek a court determination rather than unilaterally disclosing or filing the materials elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of violating a protective order (contempt and related findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of the protective order (e.g., filing confidential documents in another forum without required protections) can lead to a contempt finding and related court sanctions; the district court found TCS in contempt in part because confidential documents were filed in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners whose actions contribute to unauthorized disclosures may be implicated in contempt and sanctions even if not personally held in contempt by the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to confirm confidentiality before submitting documents to USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners who assemble and file IDSs should confirm whether documents are subject to protective orders and whether the confidentiality has been properly preserved before submitting them to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's stated belief that confidentiality had been waived did not substitute for affirmative steps (e.g., court determination or following MPEP filing procedures) to ensure confidentiality was appropriately handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obtain court guidance when unsure about protective-order applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner is uncertain whether documents are covered by a protective order, the practitioner should seek guidance from the district court prior to disclosing the documents to third parties or submitting them in another proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order highlights that failing to obtain such guidance, and instead forwarding documents for filing, contributed to the disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling a legal matter without adequate preparation (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing or handling a legal matter without preparation adequate in the circumstances constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b) and is sanctionable by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent admitted there was sufficient evidence that his conduct in preparing and causing the IDS to be filed satisfied the elements of § 10.77(b); lack of due diligence in handling confidential materials can meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and publication for admitted/proved professional misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions for disciplinary violations may include public reprimand, publication of the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette, and consideration of the record in future disciplinary matters as an aggravating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement ordered a public reprimand, publication of the Final Order and Official Gazette notice, and preserved the Office's ability to consider the record in future proceedings; parties also bear their own costs unless otherwise agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement procedure and dismissal mechanics in resolved disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement agreement resolving disciplinary action may be approved by the Under Secretary/Director, include stipulated facts and agreed sanctions, and the OED Director may be ordered to file a motion to dismiss the pending disciplinary proceeding within a specified time (here, 30 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlements can resolve proceedings while preserving the Office's ability to use the record later; the Final Order specified procedural steps for implementing the settlement (publication, dismissal motion, costs).
